sectors.trend: Gold discoveries across WA (Gateway, King River 44g/t, Moonlight, PLC Murchison) and True North's Qld copper expansion provide sector support. Coal booms domestically. Lithium exploration (ZhongNuo/Chariot in Nigeria) signals diversification. However, oil-driven inflation may pressure non-energy miners via higher input costs.
sectors.implications: Gold miners (GOLD.AX, NGX.AX) and coal names (BHP.AX, WDS.AX, LSE.AX) benefit from safe-haven flows and domestic demand. Copper (STO.AX, NHC.AX) supported by True North expansion. Monitor iron ore (RIO.AX, FMG.AX) for China demand signals amid global risk-off.

sectors.trend: Mortgage stress at 18-year highs and a potential fourth RBA rate hike create headwinds for NPS and credit growth. CBA fee controversy (13-year inactive card charges) damages consumer trust. Housing correction fears (10% decline) threaten loan book quality.
sectors.implications: Big Four (CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX) face margin pressure from rate sensitivity and rising NPLs. Defensive positioning warranted. Insurance (CGU.AX, WBC.AX) under scrutiny over short-changed home claims.

sectors.trend: Coal sector in domestic boom; Premier urges Chinese/Indian coal firm merger before funding stops. Chinese solar capacity surpasses coal globally, signalling structural transition. Oil prices elevated on Iran conflict.
sectors.implications: Coal producers (WDS.AX, LSE.AX, BHP.AX) benefit short-term from price support and policy urgency. LNG (WDS.AX, BHP.AX) insulated from oil volatility. Solar/renewables (SOL.AX, LIT.AX) gain from China's capacity shift.

sectors.trend: Qantas ground crews vote for strike right amid pay dispute. Per-capita recession and inflation 'home grown' squeeze household budgets. Housing affordability crisis dominates political discourse.
sectors.implications: QAN.AX faces operational risk from potential industrial action. Consumer staples (WES.AX, WOL.AX, CPL.AX) offer relative defensiveness. Housing-linked names (SGH.AX, LVH.AX) under pressure.

sectors.trend: Sydney developer Bathla warns of collapse within days; 'Evergrande moment' narrative gains traction. House prices could fall 10% on fourth rate hike. Housing affordability crisis intensifies.
sectors.implications: Property developers (DHG.AX, LVH.AX, SGH.AX) face liquidity risk. REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX, SPG.AX) pressured by higher borrowing costs. Credit quality deterioration likely.

sectors.trend: Global AI bubble concerns intensify; Iran conflict 'bombs AI bubble' narrative. Brookfield's $25B AI power framework and Nvidia/Micron dominance highlight concentration risk. Citi advises buying tumbling tech.
sectors.implications: ASX tech (WTC.AX, XRO.AX, CAR.AX) vulnerable to global risk-off. Canva (CNDF) privacy legal fight adds idiosyncratic risk. Diversification away from AI concentration advised.

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce duration exposure; favour rate-insensitive sectors (staples, healthcare); hedge with short-duration bonds

risk_assessment.mitigation: Avoid high-leverage property developers; monitor NPL trends at Big Four banks; favour listed infrastructure over residential REITs

risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge energy exposure; favour domestic coal/LNG over oil importers; monitor AUD/USD for inflation pass-through

risk_assessment.mitigation: Diversify away from concentrated AI exposure; favour cash-generative tech over growth-at-any-cost names

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain under pressure over 1–3 months as RBA fourth hike, oil-driven inflation, and housing stress dominate. ^AXJO may test lower supports. Materials (gold, coal) and defensives (healthcare, staples) outperform. Property and high-beta tech lag. Qantas strike risk adds volatility.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautiously constructive if RBA pivots post-hike cycle. Productivity concerns ('bad to worse') cap earnings growth. Coal-to-solar transition creates structural winners/losers. Gold and copper exploration pipeline supports materials sector. Housing correction, if it materialises, will be a multi-quarter drag on financials and construction.
